title: Het perfectum met hebben
summary: The everyday past: hebben + a ge-…-t/-d participle, and the 't kofschip rule

blocks.title: Het perfectum — de dagelijkse verleden tijd
blocks.body: Dutch tells most everyday past stories with the **perfect tense**: a form of *hebben* in second position, and a **past participle** at the very end. *Ik heb gisteren gewerkt.* (I worked yesterday.) The *heb* holds the V2 spot; *gewerkt* waits at the end. Where English says just "worked", Dutch says "have worked" for the same everyday past.
blocks.callout: The participle always parks at the very end — even in a long sentence: *Ik heb gisteren de hele dag gewerkt.*

blocks.title: ge- + stam + -t of -d
blocks.body: Build a regular participle from three parts: **ge-** + the **stem** + **-t or -d**. The stem is the infinitive minus *-en* (*werken* → *werk*). Choose the ending with **'t kofschip**: if the stem ends in one of the voiceless sounds **t, k, f, s, ch, p**, add **-t**. Otherwise add **-d**.

rows: t, k, f, s, ch, p ('t kofschip)
iets anders (l, r, n, m, klinker)

blocks.callout: Memory hook: the nonsense word *'t kofschip* hides every voiceless letter — k, f, s, ch, p (plus t).

blocks.title: De deelwoorden — tik om te horen

pairs.note: werk ends in k (kofschip) → -t; speel ends in l → -d.
fiets ends in s → -t; hoor ends in r → -d.
kook ends in k → -t; woon ends in n → -d.

blocks.explain: *maak* ends in **k** — a 't kofschip letter — so the ending is **-t**: *gemaakt*. (*maakte* is next week's imperfect.)

blocks.hint: The stem kook ends in k → 't kofschip.
blocks.explain: gekookt. Stem *kook* ends in k, so the ending is -t.

blocks.hint: heb in second position, participle at the end.
blocks.explain: *Ik heb gisteren gefietst.* — heb second, *gefietst* at the end. Front the time word and it inverts: *Gisteren heb ik gefietst.*

blocks.prompt: Wat heb je gisteren gedaan? Write three things you did yesterday, each with *ik heb* + a participle.
